newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO's Arafat summons diplomats over peace crisis.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Arafat summons diplomats over peace crisis.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Tuesday invited diplomats from countries involved in Middle East peace moves for a meeting to discuss the crisis in Israeli-PLO negotiations, an aide said.

Arafat spokesman Nabil Abu Rdainah said the meeting to be held later this week would "assess the peace process in its entirety and the crisis in the negotiations resulting from the Israeli practices."
Abu Rdainah said Arafat intended to ask the countries "to shoulder their responsibilities towards the peace process."

Saeb Erekat, a top PLO negotiator, said Arafat had invited representatives from the United States, Russia, the European Union, Egypt, Jordan, Japan and Norway to the meeting to be held in self-ruled Gaza on Saturday.

Palestinians said the peace process had plunged into crisis after an Israeli cabinet decision on Friday to hand over only a third of the West Bank land they had expected in an Israeli troop redeployment due last week.
Arafat spurned the Israeli decision to hand over another nine percent of the West Bank to his self-rule authority. Palestinians expected 30 percent.

The Israeli pullback decision added fuel to Palestinian rage, already burning over Israel's plans to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem and to close down four Palestinian institutions in the city which it says are run by the Palestinian Authority.
